neighbours.label: link word (by / for / to) that ties a predicate to a following verb of means or purpose: 'made up for it by staying', 'praised for developing', 'worn to protect'
fire: He made up for his poor grades by working twice as hard the following year.
A gaiter is a covering worn to keep mud and water out of the boot.
The Phoenicians are remembered for spreading the alphabet around the Mediterranean.
She made amends for the broken vase by baking her aunt a cake.
An apron is a garment worn to shield the clothes from flour and grease.
The Babylonians are admired for charting the movements of the planets.
The team compensated for its small budget by borrowing equipment from the university.
The Dutch are celebrated for reclaiming large areas of land from the sea.
quiet: He was praised for his good grades by the head teacher the following year.
A gaiter is a covering for the lower leg, common among hikers.
The Phoenicians are remembered for their alphabet and their purple dye.
She was forgiven for the broken vase by her aunt after a week.
An apron is a garment with a bib and two long strings at the waist.
The Babylonians are admired for their careful records of the planets.
The team was given a small budget by the university for new equipment.
The Dutch are celebrated for their dikes, canals and windmills.

notes: Card flags the pole broad (2.4%) with a gate-closed regime for 81% of its mass; the top 32 peak on ' to' x5, ' of' x4, ' as' x2, ' by' x2, ' =='. Probes: 'by staying' 0.52, '==' in an assert 0.52, 'inventing' 0.49, 'worn to' 0.26-0.34, 'for developing' 0.25; the same prepositions before a noun 0.02-0.04, 'used to separate' 0.05. A list-like label for a low-magnitude pole; near misses keep the preposition but follow it with a noun.
